subject: Draft Order Form — pricing buckets & go-live trigger
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acmeinc.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Liang <tom.liang@acmeinc.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Dec 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft order form + pricing buckets — initial redlines

Markus / Ben,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Our procurement team did a quick pass and attached a tracked-redline with three main asks: we want the go-live activation tied to a specific acceptance milestone (rather than calendar-based), the pricing buckets need clearer language on usage bands and overage calculation, and we need a clearer statement on which entity is responsible for VAT in cross-border usage.

I attached the redline and a short summary (redline-summary-20281213.pdf) showing the two clauses we think will be non-negotiable for our accounting team. Can your legal ops confirm whether Redwood can accept an acceptance-based commencement and provide a payment schedule that aligns with milestone sign-offs?

Also looping in Tom from Acme procurement — Tom, can you confirm whether Acme is able to provide a single billing entity for the first 12 months or whether we should expect multiple entities?

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Director, Strategic Procurement
Acme, Inc.

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_Redline_20281213.docx (document/redline), redline-summary-20281213.pdf (application/pdf)

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acmeinc.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 Dec 2028 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft order form + pricing buckets — initial redlines

Ellen — really appreciate the quick read and the clear summary. High level: we can probably accept an acceptance-based commencement, but we need to narrow the acceptance criteria and add a fall-back automatic commencement date after X days to avoid open-ended liability.

Ben / Grace — can you draft a payment schedule that ties milestone invoices to the acceptance checklist Ellen shared, and show the impact on revenue recognition? If we push acceptance-based commencement we should carve an automatic start for accounting purposes (suggest: 30 days after delivery if no acceptance recorded).

Kimberly — Ben flagged several redlines in pricing-band language; can Legal Ops review the attached and confirm if we can accept Acme's overage calculation (they want % overage billed at a blended rate rather than per-token). If not acceptable, propose alternative wording that preserves our unit economics.

Ellen / Tom — we'll come back with proposed wording by EOD tomorrow. In the meantime, could you clarify whether VAT should be the customer's responsibility or if Acme expects Redwood to invoice VAT separately? That will change the order form appendix.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft order form + pricing buckets — legal redlines and fallback language

Team — I reviewed Acme's redline and added comments to the attached Word document. Summary of our position: 1) Acceptance-based commencement is acceptable provided the acceptance criteria are explicit (functionality checklist + 7-business-day cure period) and we add an automatic commencement date (we propose: 30 days after delivery). 2) Overage billing: we cannot accept their "blended" overage without a clear definition of the blended calculation; propose instead a defined per-unit overage rate with a monthly reconciliation clause. 3) VAT/residency: request that Acme confirm billing entity; absent confirmation, Redwood will bill without VAT and Acme will self-assess (we can discuss reverse-charge in EU).

I've drafted alternate wording for sections 2.1 (Commencement), 3.4 (Pricing bands & overage), and Appendix B (Tax handling). I also flagged an indemnity carveout around third-party model licensing — Simon from external counsel, please see the flagged language and advise if this changes the commercial exposure materially.

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_Redline_20281213.docx (updated with comments)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Legal Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acmeinc.com>

Cc: Tom Liang <tom.liang@acmeinc.com>, Simon Reed <simon.reed@lawfirm.co>
Date: Fri, 14 Dec 2028 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft order form + pricing buckets — follow-up on VAT and billing entity

Markus / Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed fallbacks. Tom confirms Acme intends to invoice from a single US entity for year one; they will provide billing details on Monday. Regarding VAT, Acme expects to be responsible for VAT/self-assessment; they prefer Redwood not to add VAT to the invoice.

Tom also asked whether Redwood can provide a short schedule showing estimated payments tied to the acceptance milestones (a simple table with expected invoice dates and amounts). That will help Finance sign-off.

If Simon has any concerns about the indemnity carveout, please flag them — otherwise we intend to accept the revised commencement language with the automatic 30-day fallback.

Best,
Ellen

If that aligns, we'll prepare a final tracked-redline for signature and route it to Legal for DocuSign.
